title: Kapukai Visual Pattern Library
scope: These are design questions, not findings about every institution or proof of intent. Sources support the underlying principles; the tests are proposed here.

patterns.title: Correction must reach the consequence
patterns.insight: A correction may arrive at the source while consequences continue wherever the earlier information traveled.
patterns.observe: Trace one accepted correction through every known recipient that used the earlier information.
patterns.measure: Compare recipients updated, restrictions removed, and elapsed time with the original information’s reach.
patterns.repair: Assign correction owners, confirm recipient updates, and check whether downstream consequences actually end.
patterns.tradeoff: Fast propagation helps timely action; it also needs reliable correction paths and limits on unnecessary sharing.
patterns.evidence_needed: Recipient lists, correction decisions, delivery acknowledgments, updated records, and evidence that downstream restrictions changed.
patterns.counterexample: Every affected recipient updates promptly, and verified consequences end without the obsolete information reappearing.
patterns.image_description: Illustrative paired networks: an original decision reaches several recipients; the correction route must reach each place where consequences persist.

patterns.title: The unowned handoff
patterns.insight: A referral can move the paperwork without transferring responsibility for the next decision.
patterns.observe: At each transfer, identify who accepts the task and who can resolve a stalled handoff.
patterns.measure: Count transfers without acknowledgment, unresolved ownership disputes, and time spent waiting between offices.
patterns.repair: Name the receiving owner, require acceptance, and define escalation when responsibility remains disputed.
patterns.tradeoff: Specialization can improve decisions, but additional handoffs need explicit responsibility and enough context.
patterns.evidence_needed: Transfer logs, acceptance records, delegated authority, escalation rules, and elapsed time between responsible owners.
patterns.counterexample: A referral is accepted by a named owner who has authority and resources to resolve it.
patterns.image_description: Illustrative handoff between offices: a referral reaches a boundary, but responsibility must be accepted by a receiving owner.

patterns.title: Copies are not independent corroboration
patterns.insight: Several matching records may repeat one assertion rather than provide several independent reasons to believe it.
patterns.observe: Follow each supporting record back to its originating evidence and later transformations.
patterns.measure: Count independent source observations separately from copies, summaries, and records derived from the same source.
patterns.repair: Preserve provenance and distinguish independent support from repeated claims before weighing the evidence.
patterns.tradeoff: Sharing improves access, but repetition must not be treated as additional independent evidence.
patterns.evidence_needed: Original observations, source identifiers, derivation history, timestamps, and reasons for treating sources as independent.
patterns.counterexample: Matching records come from separate observations with independent evidentiary support.
patterns.image_description: Illustrative provenance network: one source is copied into several records; copies are distinguished from independent observations.

patterns.title: Labels outrun their evidence
patterns.insight: A tentative label can acquire greater authority as it travels even when its supporting evidence has not changed.
patterns.observe: Track where an allegation, provisional assessment, or confirmed finding changes category or triggers a stronger response.
patterns.measure: Count escalations without a traceable evidentiary basis, applicable rule, or authorized review.
patterns.repair: Keep allegations, assessments, and findings distinct; require evidence and authorized review before changing status.
patterns.tradeoff: Early warnings can support protection; provisional status and timely review help limit unsupported consequences.
patterns.evidence_needed: Original wording, status changes, supporting evidence, applicable criteria, authorizations, and triggered actions.
patterns.counterexample: A stronger classification follows new evidence and documented review under the applicable rule.
patterns.image_description: Illustrative label history: a provisional assertion becomes a stronger classification without visible new support, prompting an evidence check.

patterns.title: Closed ticket, unresolved consequence
patterns.insight: Closing a complaint or completing a task does not, by itself, show that the underlying problem was repaired.
patterns.observe: Check the affected person’s situation after administrative closure, including any continuing restrictions.
patterns.measure: Report closure separately from verified repair, time to relief, and recurrence of the same problem.
patterns.repair: Define the outcome required for resolution, verify it, and reopen cases when the problem persists.
patterns.tradeoff: Outcome verification takes resources; prioritize serious consequences and avoid making affected people repeatedly prove the same unresolved harm.
patterns.evidence_needed: Closure criteria, follow-up records, restored access, remaining restrictions, and recurrence checks.
patterns.counterexample: Closure follows verified repair, and later monitoring finds no continuing consequence from the original error.
patterns.image_description: Illustrative outcome chain: administrative closure is separated from verified restoration of the affected person’s situation.

patterns.title: Less burden. Effective protection.
patterns.insight: A procedural step should be judged by the protection it provides alongside the effort and delay it imposes.
patterns.observe: Ask what risk each requirement addresses and who bears its time, cost, and accessibility demands.
patterns.measure: Compare errors prevented with completion time, repeated submissions, abandonment, and unequal access.
patterns.repair: Remove duplication, offer accessible routes, and retain safeguards that demonstrably protect rights or public interests.
patterns.tradeoff: Simplification can remove friction or remove protection; assess both before changing a requirement.
patterns.evidence_needed: Requirement purpose, completion and abandonment data, user effort, accessibility evidence, and measured protection.
patterns.counterexample: A demanding requirement demonstrably prevents serious harm, with accessible assistance and proportionate exceptions.
patterns.image_description: A conceptual two-axis matrix comparing procedural burden and verified protection. No agencies or measured values are plotted.

patterns.title: Independent review, connected repair
patterns.insight: Independent review needs connected repair and a clearly assigned, lawful route to interim protection where available.
patterns.observe: Who has lawful authority to pause harmful action pending review, under what conditions and response time?
patterns.measure: Track pause requests, response times, review dates, justified refusals, and whether authorized relief reaches every responsible office.
patterns.repair: Preserve independent review; define lawful pause conditions, deadlines, review, and connected repair without unnecessary data sharing.
patterns.tradeoff: A pause can prevent worsening harm or interrupt needed protection; define proportionate conditions and prompt review.
patterns.evidence_needed: Governing authority, pause criteria, request logs, reasons, review deadlines, and evidence of downstream implementation.
patterns.counterexample: A boundary preserves impartial review while a separately authorized official promptly implements temporary relief.
patterns.image_description: A conceptual map preserving independent review while connecting authorized interim protection and implementation of a remedy.

patterns.title: Metrics shape choices
patterns.insight: Targets can direct attention toward fast completion while leaving accuracy, access, or lasting repair less visible.
patterns.observe: Compare rewarded targets with the outcomes the service is supposed to deliver.
patterns.measure: Review speed and volume alongside error rates, unresolved harm, repeat work, and access across groups.
patterns.repair: Balance output targets with outcome checks, review workload pressures, and investigate unexpected changes in reported performance.
patterns.tradeoff: More measures can reveal blind spots but increase reporting work; keep the set small and decision-relevant.
patterns.evidence_needed: Target definitions, performance reviews, workload data, validation samples, outcome trends, and documented responses to missed targets.
patterns.counterexample: Balanced measures reward accurate, timely outcomes, and independent checks confirm that reported improvements persist.
patterns.image_description: A conceptual feedback loop linking performance targets, staff choices, measured outputs and checks of human outcomes.

stpa-handbook-2018.label: STPA Handbook · feedback and execution
stpa-handbook-2018.scope: Analyzes missing, delayed, incorrect, and unapplied feedback; this card applies that principle to correction propagation. Calls for checking responsibilities, controls, and feedback for conflicts and gaps. Analyzes decisions based on incorrect, misinterpreted, conflicting, or missing information; label escalation is a proposed application.

w3c-prov-overview.scope: Provides a framework for recording sources, agents, processing, versioning, and derivation; the corroboration test is our application.

gao-green-book-2025.label: GAO Green Book · remediation
gao-green-book-2025.scope: Requires timely corrective action and addresses measurable remediation progress; this card proposes a person-level outcome check. Addresses excessive goal-related pressures and whether measures appropriately evaluate objectives.

oecd-regulatory-policy-governance.scope: Recommends reducing unnecessary burdens while preserving legitimate objectives and evaluating public outcomes.
